body:
Review pass 2 - Epic 1 in progress (support index).

GOOD: .volume_ball_membership is the right algorithm and the numbers are excellent - vectorised over stencil offsets, linear, 97,336 voxels in 2.35s (24 us/voxel, radius 6.1mm at 3mm spacing). Epic 1's 50-60k target is comfortably met on the volume path.

CONCERN filed as bd-01KZXBT2GF4E4W9N685KAHAYER (p1): .coordinate_ball_members still carries a quadratic term. It splits on CHARACTER cell keys and does groups[candidate_keys] per centre, so each centre costs O(n_groups) via match() and the total is O(p x n_groups).

  coordinate_cells:  p=8000 1.29s (162 us/vox) | p=27000 6.29s (233) | p=50653 14.55s (287)
  volume_stencil:    p=8000 0.50s ( 62 us/vox) | p=27000 0.69s ( 26) | p=97336 2.35s ( 24)

At p=8000 the new coordinate provider is only ~1.5x faster than the all-pairs loop it replaced (1.89s). Discriminating test - hold p=19683, vary radius so only n_groups changes: lookup-only cost is 8.49s at n_groups=15625 vs 2.31s at n_groups=343, i.e. it tracks n_groups, not support size. Small radii are worst: 11.6s to build supports averaging 6.8 voxels.

This is not caught today because test-support-index.R:125 runs the 50k fixture through volume_domain and asserts pair_pattern_nnz < p^2/1000 - a storage bound. Epic 1 acceptance says 'without quadratic-in-p allocation', so runtime is ungated and coordinate_cells is only covered by the small fixture at line 24.

Fix: integer cell codes + one vectorised match() across all centres (or order()/rle bucketing) -> O(p k). Then scale-test both providers. Worth doing because the README headline example uses abstract_domain(), which routes here.

Minor: R/frame.R:115 uses exists('support_index', inherits = FALSE) to detect the branch - correct today, fragile; prefer NULL-init. And voxels()/regions()/whole_brain() carry no support_index yet, so 'one canonical support topology' is searchlight-only so far.

Still open from pass 1 and unacked:  frame/metric composition (p0) and  K-inverse handle action.
